about: The curated deck factory works through this list from the top. See docs/curated-themes/factory.md.

themes.name: English History
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of English history, Stonehenge to the present

themes.name: Indonesia
themes.scope: Yes if it happened in what is now Indonesia

themes.name: Kings of England
themes.scope: Yes if it is a monarch's accession, death or defining act

themes.name: Assassinations
themes.scope: Yes if a named person was killed for political reasons

themes.name: Automata
themes.scope: Yes if it is a machine built to act on its own

themes.name: Codes & Ciphers
themes.scope: Yes if it makes or breaks secret writing

themes.name: Clockwork
themes.scope: Yes if it is a device or convention for measuring time

themes.name: Cosmic Ideas
themes.scope: Yes if it is an idea about what the universe is

themes.name: Bridges & Tunnels
themes.scope: Yes if it is a built crossing of water, valley or rock

themes.name: Eureka Moments
themes.scope: Yes if it is the specific moment a discovery landed

themes.name: The Games Board
themes.scope: Yes if it is a game played at a table, or a machine that beat us at one

themes.name: Let There Be Light
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of making artificial light

themes.name: Lost & Found
themes.scope: Yes if something buried was found, or a dead script read

themes.name: Mapmakers
themes.scope: Yes if it changed what people thought the world looked like

themes.name: Hard Currency
themes.scope: Yes if it is a form of money, or the institution issuing one

themes.name: Nations of Europe
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding moment of a European country

themes.name: Numbers & Proofs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a mathematical idea entering human thought

themes.name: Plague Years
themes.scope: Yes if it is a named outbreak, or a decisive step in ending one

themes.name: The Deep
themes.scope: Yes if it is going deliberately under water, or finding what sank

themes.name: When the Earth Moved
themes.scope: Yes if it is an eruption, earthquake or tsunami

themes.name: What We Drink
themes.scope: Yes if it is a drink made on purpose, or a rule about drinking it

themes.name: Before Us
themes.scope: Yes if it happened before Homo sapiens existed

themes.name: Capitals Founded
themes.scope: Yes if it founded a city that is a national capital today

themes.name: Cities Ablaze
themes.scope: Yes if a city burned, or it is a step in fighting urban fire

themes.name: Ends of the Earth
themes.scope: Yes if people first reached a pole, a summit or an unvisited extreme

themes.name: Famine Years
themes.scope: Yes if it is a named famine, or a decisive step in ending one

themes.name: Mandate of Heaven
themes.scope: Yes if it is a Chinese dynasty's founding, peak act or fall

themes.name: On Stage
themes.scope: Yes if it is a stage form, a landmark premiere or a famous playhouse

themes.name: Peace at Last
themes.scope: Yes if it is a treaty or armistice that ended a named war

themes.name: Pharaohs
themes.scope: Yes if it is an act of an Egyptian ruler, Narmer to Cleopatra

themes.name: Pirates & Privateers
themes.scope: Yes if it is armed robbery at sea, or the war on it

themes.name: Places of Learning
themes.scope: Yes if it founded or destroyed a school, university or great library

themes.name: Sail & Steam
themes.scope: Yes if it is a new kind of ship, or one vessel that changed seafaring

themes.name: Stolen!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous theft, robbery or fraud carried out for gain

themes.name: Taking Flight
themes.scope: Yes if a person left the ground in a craft (atmosphere only)

themes.name: Tallest in the World
themes.scope: Yes if it became the tallest structure of its day, or let us build up

themes.name: Tamed
themes.scope: Yes if it is an animal brought into human service

themes.name: The First Woman
themes.scope: Yes if it is the first time a woman did or held something

themes.name: The Roman Story
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of the Roman state, to 1453

themes.name: Under Siege
themes.scope: Yes if it is the siege of a named city or fortress

themes.name: Under the Knife
themes.scope: Yes if it is a surgical procedure or tool, or a way to survive one

themes.name: Walls & Fortresses
themes.scope: Yes if it built or brought down a fortification meant to keep people out

themes.name: Waterworks
themes.scope: Yes if it moves or holds back water by design

themes.name: Chains Broken
themes.scope: Yes if it is the abolition of slavery or serfdom in a country or empire, or a decisive act of the abolition struggle
themes.boundary: Chains Broken: the end of slavery and serfdom; revolts by the enslaved go to Rise Up!, US civil rights after 1896 to Civil Rights Road, Haiti's revolution to The Liberators.

themes.name: All Aboard!
themes.scope: Yes if it is the opening of an intercity railway line, a railway first or record, or a famous train (city metros and trams excepted)
themes.boundary: All Aboard!: mainline railways; city metros and trams go to Mind the Gap, rail tunnels and bridges to Bridges & Tunnels, Siberia's settlement to Siberia.

themes.name: Wild Weather
themes.scope: Yes if it is a named or record-setting storm, flood, tornado, heatwave, freeze or smog (quakes, eruptions and famine droughts excepted)
themes.boundary: Wild Weather: weather at its worst; quakes, eruptions and tsunamis go to When the Earth Moved, famine-causing droughts to Famine Years, towns lost to fire to Cities Ablaze.

themes.name: Beautiful Game
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous football (soccer) match, goal, transfer or rule change, not the founding of a competition and not an upset
themes.boundary: Beautiful Game: football's great moments; first editions of cups go to Opening Whistle, upsets to Giant Killers, the FA's founding rules to Rule Book.
example_beats: Hand of God and Goal of the Century (1986)

themes.name: Silicon Dreams
themes.scope: Yes if it is an electronic computer, chip or piece of computing hardware first built or sold, or the founding of the firm that made it (1936 onward)
themes.boundary: Silicon Dreams: electronic hardware; mechanical calculators go to Automata, wartime codebreaking machines to Codes & Ciphers, software to Hello, World.

themes.name: Kings of Kings
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a Persian shah or Iranian dynasty's ruler, from Cyrus the Great to the last Shah (1979)
themes.boundary: Kings of Kings: Persia's rulers; Persepolis burning goes to Cities Ablaze, Thermopylae to Against the Odds, Nader Shah's sack of Delhi to Peacock Throne.
example_beats: Cyrus founds the Achaemenid Empire (550 BC)
Darius carves the Behistun inscription (520 BC)

themes.name: Boom & Bust
themes.scope: Yes if it is a financial bubble, crash, panic or bank failure
themes.boundary: Boom & Bust: markets breaking; the South Sea Bubble and other frauds stay with Stolen!, currencies and hyperinflation with Hard Currency, tulips as plants to Plant Hunters.

themes.name: Scramble for Africa
themes.scope: Yes if it is an outsider's expedition into Africa, or a claim, treaty, conquest or act of resistance there, 1788 to 1914
themes.boundary: Scramble for Africa: exploration and conquest by outsiders, and the resistance to it; African states' own story goes to African Kingdoms, independence to Uhuru, the Suez Canal to Bridges & Tunnels.
themes.probe: livingstone|\bstanley\b|mungo park|\bspeke\b|source of the nile|berlin conference|scramble for africa|congo free state|fashoda|\badwa\b|isandlwana|maji maji|boer war

themes.name: Houses of Worship
themes.scope: Yes if it is the building, consecration or completion of a world-famous temple, church, mosque, synagogue or shrine
themes.boundary: Houses of Worship: sacred buildings; spires that set height records go to Tallest in the World, Angkor Wat to Temple Kingdoms, the Dome of the Rock to The Caliphs, Hagia Sophia to The Roman Story.

themes.name: Lift-Off!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a rocket or launch vehicle's first flight, record or breakthrough (the machine, not the mission)
themes.boundary: Lift-Off!: rockets as machines, from fire arrows to reusable boosters; what they carried goes to Into Orbit and Other Worlds, guns and cannon to Powder & Shot.

themes.name: Between the Rivers
themes.scope: Yes if it is an event of ancient Mesopotamia (Sumer, Akkad, Babylon, Assyria), from Uruk to the Persian conquest (539 BC)
themes.boundary: Between the Rivers: Sumer to Babylon's fall; Persia from Cyrus on goes to Kings of Kings, sieges like Lachish to Under Siege, Ashurbanipal's library to Places of Learning, Egypt to Pharaohs.
example_beats: Uruk becomes the first city (c. 3500 BC)
Sargon of Akkad founds his empire (2334 BC)
Sennacherib builds his Nineveh palace (700 BC)

themes.name: Gallery Greats
themes.scope: Yes if it is a single, individually famous painting, drawing or print from outside Japan, dated to its completion
themes.boundary: Gallery Greats: one famous picture; statues and memorials go to Unveiled!, the movements behind them to Isms, their thefts to Stolen!

themes.name: Household Gadgets
themes.scope: Yes if it is a domestic appliance or home gadget first sold or patented
themes.boundary: Household Gadgets: machines for the home; lighting goes to Let There Be Light, food preserving to Food Tech, portable gadgets to In Your Pocket.
example_beats: Mechanical dishwasher patented by Josephine Cochrane (1886)

themes.name: Faith Founded
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a religion, denomination, monastic order or major religious movement
themes.boundary: Faith Founded: new faiths and orders; popes and church councils go to Habemus Papam, Buddhism's spread to Buddha's Path, the caliphs to The Caliphs.
example_beats: Joseph Smith founds the Church of Christ (1830)

themes.name: Horseless Carriages
themes.scope: Yes if it is the launch of a famous car model or carmaker, or a motoring first (electric cars included)
themes.boundary: Horseless Carriages: cars; roads and traffic rules go to The Open Road, the moving assembly line to Made by Machine, motorbikes to Two Wheels.

themes.name: Landfall!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a voyage between 1400 and 1800 that first reached or charted a named coast, strait, river mouth or island group outside the Pacific
themes.boundary: Landfall!: the age of sail's arrivals outside the Pacific; Pacific crossings go to Pacific Voyagers, the colonies that followed to Flag Planted, first settlement of empty islands to Ends of the Earth.
example_beats: Hudson sails up the Hudson River (1609)
Dirk Hartog lands on Australia's west coast (1616)

themes.name: Fright Night
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark horror novel, story, film or game, or the debut of a famous fictional monster
themes.boundary: Fright Night: works made to frighten; science fiction and fantasy go to Beyond the Stars, detective fiction to Whodunit, real-life sightings to Monster Sightings.

themes.name: Crowned Queens
themes.scope: Yes if it is the accession or defining act of a woman ruling in her own right as queen, empress, regent or sultana, outside England, Britain and ancient Egypt
themes.boundary: Crowned Queens: women who ruled; English and British queens go to Kings of England, Hatshepsut and Cleopatra to Pharaohs, Wu Zetian to The First Woman.
example_beats: Irene becomes sole ruler of Byzantium (797)
Razia Sultana takes the Delhi throne (1236)
Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands (1740)

themes.name: Hello, World
themes.scope: Yes if it is a programming language, operating system or landmark piece of software being created or released
themes.boundary: Hello, World: software; the machines go to Silicon Dreams, the web and browsers to Going Online, AI systems to Thinking Machines, Lovelace and Hopper stay with The First Woman.

themes.name: Modern Marvels
themes.scope: Yes if it is a building opened since 1900 that is celebrated for its design and was never the world's tallest or a museum
themes.boundary: Modern Marvels: landmark modern design; record-height towers go to Tallest in the World, museums to Doors Open, expo pavilions to Expo Fever.

themes.name: Mongol Storm
themes.scope: Yes if it is a conquest, ruler or campaign of the Mongol empire, its khanates or Timur, 1206 to 1405
themes.boundary: Mongol Storm: Genghis to Timur; the steppe before 1206 goes to Horse Lords, the Yuan as a Chinese dynasty to Mandate of Heaven, the sack of Baghdad to Under Siege.
example_beats: Kamikaze typhoon scatters the Mongol fleet (1281)

themes.name: Gold Medal Moments
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment, record or first at a modern Olympic or Paralympic Games, one per Games
themes.boundary: Gold Medal Moments: anything at the Olympics, upsets included; records set elsewhere go to Magic Numbers, upsets elsewhere to Giant Killers.
example_beats: Spyridon Louis wins the first marathon (1896)
Charlotte Cooper, first female Olympic champion (1900)
Jim Thorpe's pentathlon and decathlon wins (1912)
Abebe Bikila runs barefoot to marathon gold (1960)
Miracle on Ice at Lake Placid (1980)

themes.name: Doors Open
themes.scope: Yes if it is the opening of a famous museum or gallery to the public
themes.boundary: Doors Open: museums and galleries, buildings included; schools and libraries go to Places of Learning, other landmark modern buildings to Modern Marvels.
example_beats: The Louvre opens as a public museum (1793)

themes.name: Newfound Beasts
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous animal species first scientifically described, filmed or found alive
themes.boundary: Newfound Beasts: species new to science; famous individual animals go to Famous Animals, fossils to Bone Hunters, vent life to The Deep.

themes.name: Still Trading
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a company, shop or brand that still trades today and was founded before 1800
themes.boundary: Still Trading: the world's oldest firms; younger brands go to the theme for what they sell (Sweet Tooth, Horseless Carriages), mints and central banks to Hard Currency, breweries to What We Drink.

themes.name: Material World
themes.scope: Yes if it is the invention or first production of a new material: ceramic, glass, cement, alloy, rubber or plastic (textile fibres excepted)
themes.boundary: Material World: the stuff things are made of; fibres and fabrics go to Spun Yarn, Bessemer steel to Tallest in the World, graphene to Eureka Moments.
example_beats: Aluminium made cheap by Hall and Heroult (1886)

themes.name: Pop Goes Global
themes.scope: Yes if it is a song, film, show or star from outside the English-speaking world, Japan and Korea that broke through to a worldwide audience
themes.boundary: Pop Goes Global: crossover hits from Latin America, Africa, India, China and Europe; Korea goes to Korean Wave, Japan to Cool Japan, the birth of genres to Born to Groove.
example_beats: Bruce Lee in Enter the Dragon (1973)
Escrava Isaura goes global on TV (1976)

themes.name: When It Went Wrong
themes.scope: Yes if it is an industrial or engineering accident: an explosion, collapse, leak or dam failure (fires, nuclear accidents, oil spills and aircraft and spacecraft losses excepted)
themes.boundary: When It Went Wrong: engineering failures; fires go to Cities Ablaze, nuclear accidents to Atoms for Peace, oil spills to Black Gold.

themes.name: Evolving Ideas
themes.scope: Yes if it is a step in understanding how life changed and began: classification, evolution, extinction as fact, or the origin of life
themes.boundary: Evolving Ideas: theories of how life changed; the voyages and field work behind them go to Field Notes, fossil finds to Bone Hunters, genes to Code of Life, the Scopes trial to Day in Court.
themes.probe: \bevolution|natural selection|\bdarwin|origin of species|lamarck|extinction (is|as) (real|fact)|cuvier|linnae|taxonom|origin of life|creationis|common ancestor

themes.name: Nobel Peace Prize
themes.scope: Yes if it is the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to a named person or organisation
themes.boundary: Nobel Peace Prize: the award itself; the struggles that won it stay with their own themes, such as Against Apartheid or Civil Rights Road, the bodies it honoured to Alphabet Soup.
example_beats: Henry Dunant wins the first prize (1901)

themes.name: Banned!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a book banned, burned, put on trial or censored, or the publication that provoked it
themes.boundary: Banned!: books under attack; other famous trials go to Day in Court, destroyed libraries to Places of Learning, political classics that were never banned to Pens Over Swords.
example_beats: Alice in Wonderland banned in Hunan (1931)

themes.name: Other Worlds
themes.scope: Yes if it is a spacecraft, crewed or not, first reaching, orbiting, landing on or flying past another world
themes.boundary: Other Worlds: missions beyond Earth orbit, the Moon landings included; Earth-orbit flights go to Into Orbit, the rockets to Lift-Off!, worlds found from the ground to Planet Spotting.

themes.name: Cool Japan
themes.scope: Yes if it is a Japanese work of art or popular culture that won a worldwide following: prints, films, manga, anime, characters or music (video games excepted)
themes.boundary: Cool Japan: Japan's pop culture abroad, manga and anime included; video games go to Insert Coin, portable gadgets to In Your Pocket, the samurai age to Shogun!
example_beats: Hiroshige's Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido (1833)

themes.name: Element Hunters
themes.scope: Yes if it is the discovery or first isolation of a chemical element, the making of a new one, or the table that orders them
themes.boundary: Element Hunters: the elements and the periodic table; particles go to Inside the Atom, elements seen in starlight and forged in stars stay with Cosmic Ideas.

themes.name: Red Flags
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a communist party, movement or state, from the Manifesto (1848) to the People's Republic of China (1949)
themes.boundary: Red Flags: communism's rise to 1949; the Cold War stand-off after it goes to Iron Curtain, the Romanov fall to The Romanovs, other political books to Pens Over Swords.

themes.name: Platinum
themes.scope: Yes if it is an album that has sold 20 million or more copies worldwide, dated to its release
themes.boundary: Platinum: the best-selling albums; the birth of the styles they sold goes to Born to Groove, the concerts to Crowd Roars.
example_beats: The Dark Side of the Moon (1973)
themes.probe: \balbums?\b|best-selling record|dark side of the moon|abbey road|\bsoundtrack

themes.name: Plant Hunters
themes.scope: Yes if it is a plant or crop found, moved between continents, bred or banked in a way that changed the world
themes.boundary: Plant Hunters: plants on the move; farm machinery and fertiliser go to Plow & Harvest, tea and coffee as drinks to What We Drink, potatoes reaching Europe and China stay with Famine Years.
example_beats: Fortune smuggles tea plants from China (1848)
Wickham smuggles rubber seeds out of Brazil (1876)

themes.name: Funny Pages
themes.scope: Yes if it is the debut of a comic strip, comic book, graphic novel or comics character from outside Japan
themes.boundary: Funny Pages: comics outside Japan; manga go to Cool Japan, animated cartoons to Drawn to Life.

themes.name: Flag Planted
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of an overseas colony, trading post or treaty port by a foreign power (not a city that is a national capital today)
themes.boundary: Flag Planted: footholds abroad; the voyages that found the coasts go to Landfall!, cities now capitals to Capitals Founded, Australia's First Fleet to Convicts & Gold.
example_beats: Shanghai opens as a treaty port (1843)

themes.name: Born to Groove
themes.scope: Yes if it is the moment a popular music genre emerged, or the record or event usually credited as its birth
themes.boundary: Born to Groove: the birth of a genre; landmark concerts go to Crowd Roars, best-selling albums to Platinum, K-pop to Korean Wave.
example_beats: Original Dixieland Jazz Band cuts the first jazz record (1917)
Robert Johnson records the Delta blues (1936)
Toots and the Maytals name reggae in Do the Reggay (1968)
DJ Kool Herc's Bronx party sparks hip-hop (1973)

themes.name: Sublime Porte
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of the Ottoman state or its sultans, from Osman (1299) to the end of the sultanate (1922), sieges excepted
themes.boundary: Sublime Porte: the Ottoman story; its great sieges (Constantinople, Vienna, Malta) go to Under Siege, caliphs before 1517 to The Caliphs, Lepanto to Broadsides.

themes.name: Bugs & Breaches
themes.scope: Yes if it is a computer virus, hack, data breach, software bug or outage that made the news
themes.boundary: Bugs & Breaches: computing gone wrong; Y2K stays with Clockwork, cyber-robberies for gain go to Stolen!, code-breaking to Codes & Ciphers.
example_beats: Moth found in the Harvard Mark II, the first 'bug' (1947)
Mariner 1 lost to a software bug (1962)

themes.name: Dress Code
themes.scope: Yes if it is a garment, accessory or fashion house that changed what people wear, dated to its launch or debut
themes.boundary: Dress Code: what people wear; fibres, fabrics and sewing machines go to Spun Yarn, the advertising behind them to Sell, Sell, Sell.
example_beats: Charles Worth opens a Paris couture house (1858)

themes.name: Field Notes
themes.scope: Yes if it is a naturalist's voyage or field study, or a landmark nature book or documentary
themes.boundary: Field Notes: naturalists in the field and their books and films; theories go to Evolving Ideas, ocean exploration to The Deep, conservation to Back from the Brink.
example_beats: Merian's Metamorphosis of the Insects of Surinam (1705)
Life on Earth airs on the BBC (1979)

themes.name: Uhuru
themes.scope: Yes if it is a sub-Saharan African country gaining independence, or a decisive act of the struggle for it, 1945 to 2011 (South Africa's apartheid story excepted)
themes.boundary: Uhuru: independence south of the Sahara; apartheid goes to Against Apartheid, North Africa and Asia to Flags Come Down, the colonial conquest to Scramble for Africa.

themes.name: Famous Animals
themes.scope: Yes if it is a moment of a single, named, famous animal (working animals in service, space animals and clones excepted)
themes.boundary: Famous Animals: celebrity creatures; working dogs, war animals, Laika and Dolly stay with Tamed, the last of a species goes to Gone Forever.
example_beats: Phar Lap wins the Melbourne Cup (1930)
Elsa the lioness returns to the wild (1960)
Paul the Octopus predicts the World Cup (2010)

themes.name: Spun Yarn
themes.scope: Yes if it is a machine, dye, fibre or process that changed how cloth is made or sewn, from the flying shuttle (1733) on
themes.boundary: Spun Yarn: the machine age of cloth; finished garments go to Dress Code, plastics and alloys to Material World, other factory machines to Made by Machine.
themes.probe: flying shuttle|spinning (jenny|mule|frame)|water frame|power loom|cotton gin|sewing machine|synthetic (dye|fib)|\bmauve|\bnylon|polyester|\blycra|\bkevlar|gore-tex|\brayon|textile (mill|factory|machine)

themes.name: Bad Science
themes.scope: Yes if it is a scientific hoax, fraud, blunder or retraction, or a product sold as safe that proved harmful
themes.boundary: Bad Science: science gone wrong; cryptids and ghosts go to Monster Sightings, frauds for money such as Theranos to Stolen!, medicines that worked to Wonder Drugs.
example_beats: Vulcan, the planet that wasn't, announced (1859)

themes.name: Special Delivery
themes.scope: Yes if it is a postal, courier or parcel service, or a first in getting physical things delivered
themes.boundary: Special Delivery: carrying letters and parcels; electric messages go to Long Distance, container ships to Sail & Steam, the Universal Postal Union to Alphabet Soup.
example_beats: Royal Mail opens to the public (1635)

themes.name: Monster Sightings
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous cryptid sighting, UFO report, ghost story or paranormal hoax
themes.boundary: Monster Sightings: cryptids, UFOs and ghosts; scientific frauds go to Bad Science, horror fiction to Fright Night.
example_beats: Betty and Barney Hill abduction claim (1961)

themes.name: Temple Kingdoms
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a kingdom or ruler of mainland Southeast Asia (Khmer, Pagan, Sukhothai, Ayutthaya, Champa, Dai Viet, Lan Xang), 40 to 1885
themes.boundary: Temple Kingdoms: mainland Southeast Asia before colonial rule; the Indonesian islands go to Indonesia, independence after 1945 to Flags Come Down, Bangkok and Hanoi's founding to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: Jayavarman II founds the Khmer Empire (802)

themes.name: Votes for Women
themes.scope: Yes if it is a country or state first giving women the vote, or a decisive act of the campaign for it
themes.boundary: Votes for Women: women winning the vote; other first-time voting systems go to The Ballot Box, women's other firsts to The First Woman.
themes.probe: suffrag|women'?s (right to )?vote|votes for women|women (gain|win|get) the vote|seneca falls|19th amendment|nineteenth amendment

themes.name: Letters & Type
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in how letters are designed, printed, typed or encoded for reading
themes.boundary: Letters & Type: the look and mechanics of text; secret writing goes to Codes & Ciphers, Korea's Hangul and Jikji to Korean Wave, reference books to Look It Up.

themes.name: The Atomic Age
themes.scope: Yes if it is a nuclear weapon's development, test or use, an arms-control treaty or a nuclear close call
themes.boundary: The Atomic Age: the bomb; reactors and their accidents go to Atoms for Peace, fission's discovery stays with Eureka Moments, other Cold War crises to Iron Curtain.
themes.probe: atom(ic)? bomb|nuclear (weapons?|bomb|test|arms|war|warhead|missile)|hydrogen bomb|h-bomb|manhattan project|trinity test|hiroshima|nagasaki|test ban|non-proliferation|arms control|missile crisis

themes.name: Sell, Sell, Sell
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous advertisement, slogan, mascot or advertising milestone
themes.boundary: Sell, Sell, Sell: the pitch itself; the shops go to Retail Therapy, the oldest firms' founding to Still Trading.
example_beats: Caxton prints one of the first advertisements (1477)
Old Spice 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' (2010)

themes.name: Before Columbus
themes.scope: Yes if it is a city, state, ruler or ceremonial monument of Mesoamerica or the Andes before the Spanish arrived (1519 in Mexico, 1532 in Peru)
themes.boundary: Before Columbus: Maya, Aztec, Andean and Inca worlds before contact; the conquest goes to Conquistadors, peoples north of Mexico to Native Nations, Tenochtitlan's founding to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: San Lorenzo Olmec at their height (c. 1200 BC)
Earliest Long Count date at Tikal (292)
Pakal takes the throne at Palenque (615)

themes.name: Korean Wave
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of Korean invention, culture or soft power, from Silla's golden age to K-pop
themes.boundary: Korean Wave: Korea's gifts to the world, Hangul and K-pop included; the Korean War goes to Iron Curtain, Hansan's turtle ships to Broadsides, Seoul's founding to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: Jikji printed with movable metal type (1377)

themes.name: Retail Therapy
themes.scope: Yes if it is the opening of a famous shop, market or retail format, or a retail innovation
themes.boundary: Retail Therapy: buying things; the oldest firms go to Still Trading, advertising to Sell, Sell, Sell, money and credit cards to Hard Currency.

themes.name: Meiji Leap
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in Japan's opening and modernisation, from Perry's arrival (1853) to the Meiji Emperor's death (1912)
themes.boundary: Meiji Leap: Japan 1853 to 1912; the samurai age before goes to Shogun!, the Meiji Constitution to Founding Documents, Tsushima to Broadsides.
example_beats: Harris Treaty opens Japan to trade (1858)
themes.probe: \bmeiji|black ships|commodore perry|matthew perry|iwakura|satsuma rebellion|rokumeikan|sino-japanese war|russo-japanese war

themes.name: Day in Court
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous trial or a landmark court ruling that changed law or public opinion (US civil-rights rulings and trials of books excepted)
themes.boundary: Day in Court: the courtroom; civil-rights rulings go to Civil Rights Road, trials of books to Banned!, police and prisons to Crime & Punishment.

themes.name: Expo Fever
themes.scope: Yes if it is a World's Fair or international exposition, dated to when it opened
themes.boundary: Expo Fever: the fairs themselves; the record towers they left go to Tallest in the World, rides to Thrill Rides, lasting modern buildings to Modern Marvels.
example_beats: Great Exhibition at the Crystal Palace (1851)
New York World's Fair, 'World of Tomorrow' (1939)

themes.name: Red-Letter Days
themes.scope: Yes if it is the creation or first observance of a holiday or festive custom kept in many places
themes.boundary: Red-Letter Days: holidays and customs; festivals staged in one place go to Party Starter, calendars and daylight saving to Clockwork, May Day's labour origins to Down Tools.
example_beats: Christmas tree popularised by Victoria and Albert (1848)

themes.name: Plow & Harvest
themes.scope: Yes if it is an invention, technique or scientific breakthrough used on a farm to grow crops or raise livestock more productively (irrigation excepted)
themes.boundary: Plow & Harvest: farm tools and science; irrigation goes to Waterworks, crops moving between continents go to Plant Hunters, Haber's fertiliser and the Green Revolution stay with Famine Years, food factories to Food Tech.

themes.name: Lines on a Map
themes.scope: Yes if it is a border drawn or redrawn, or a territory sold, swapped or partitioned, by agreement rather than by a war-ending treaty

Orson Welles' War of the Worlds broadcast (1938)
Our World, the first global satellite broadcast (1967)

themes.name: Iron Curtain
themes.scope: Yes if it is a crisis, proxy war, flashpoint or treaty between the Cold War blocs, 1946 to 1991 (the nuclear stand-off itself excepted)
themes.boundary: Iron Curtain: the blocs' confrontation; bombs and arms treaties go to The Atomic Age, the Berlin Wall stays with Walls & Fortresses, spies to Spy Games.

themes.name: Press Play
themes.scope: Yes if it is a format or machine for recording or playing back sound, from phonograph to streaming, other than a portable personal player
themes.boundary: Press Play: recording media and home playback; Walkman-style portables go to In Your Pocket, radio broadcasting to Tune In, the instruments recorded to Strike a Chord.
example_beats: First coin-operated jukebox in San Francisco (1889)

themes.name: Face to Face
themes.scope: Yes if it is a summit or congress of rulers, or an envoy or embassy sent from one court to another
themes.boundary: Face to Face: meetings and missions; the treaties that ended wars go to Peace at Last, Cold War crises to Iron Curtain, merchants and pilgrims on the caravan roads to Silk Road.
example_beats: Ibn Fadlan's embassy to the Volga (921)
Field of the Cloth of Gold (1520)

themes.name: Siberia
themes.scope: Yes if it is an expedition, settlement, exile, discovery or project in Siberia or the Russian Far East
themes.boundary: Siberia: Russia east of the Urals; the Romanov court goes to The Romanovs, the Tunguska blast to Sky Show, the Trans-Siberian line to All Aboard!
example_beats: Coldest inhabited place recorded at Oymyakon (1933)

themes.name: Shogun!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of Japan's warrior age, from the first shogunate (1185) to Perry's arrival (1853), Sengoku warlords and unifiers included
themes.boundary: Shogun!: samurai rule up to 1853; Perry's Black Ships and everything after go to Meiji Leap, Japanese pop culture to Cool Japan, the Mongol invasions to Mongol Storm.

themes.name: Long Distance
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of sending a message from one person to another across distance: semaphore, telegraph, telephone, cable, fax or satellite link (broadcasting excepted)
themes.boundary: Long Distance: point-to-point messages; broadcasting to the public goes to Tune In, the post to Special Delivery, the internet to Going Online, the first undersea cable to The Deep.
example_beats: Telstar relays TV across the Atlantic (1962)

themes.name: Strike It Rich
themes.scope: Yes if it is a gold, silver or diamond strike, rush or major find
themes.boundary: Strike It Rich: rushes for gold, silver and gems; oil strikes go to Black Gold, Australia's Eureka Stockade to Convicts & Gold, the conquest that found Potosi to Conquistadors.

themes.name: Bone Hunters
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous fossil or hominin find, or the naming of a dinosaur, dated to the find
themes.boundary: Bone Hunters: finding fossils; what they reveal about life before us goes to Before Us, human-made finds to Lost & Found, Java Man stays with Indonesia.
example_beats: Neanderthal found in the Neander valley (1856)

themes.name: Bedtime Stories
themes.scope: Yes if it is the first publication of a children's book or tale collection that is still loved
themes.boundary: Bedtime Stories: books for children, children's fantasy included; fantasy for adults goes to Beyond the Stars, toys of the characters to Toy Box.
example_beats: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997)

themes.name: Forecast!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a tool, scale, service or breakthrough for measuring, forecasting or naming weather
themes.boundary: Forecast!: reading and predicting weather; the storms themselves go to Wild Weather, climate change to Heating Up, earthquake scales to Reading the Rocks.
example_beats: FitzRoy issues the first public forecast (1861)

themes.name: Isms
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding exhibition, manifesto or group of a named art movement
themes.boundary: Isms: the launch of a movement; single famous paintings go to Gallery Greats, modern buildings to Modern Marvels.

themes.name: Going Online
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in building the internet or the web: networks, protocols, email, browsers, search, online shops and encyclopedias (social media excepted)
themes.boundary: Going Online: the net's plumbing and first services; social platforms and viral moments go to Gone Viral, hacks to Bugs & Breaches, phones to In Your Pocket.

themes.name: Inside the Mind
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark in psychology, psychiatry or brain science, psychiatric drugs included
themes.boundary: Inside the Mind: psychology and the brain; brain scanners as tools go to Seeing Inside, lobotomy and other surgery to Under the Knife, other medicines to Wonder Drugs.

themes.name: Crowd Roars
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous single concert or music festival, dated to when it was held
themes.boundary: Crowd Roars: one dated performance or music festival; carnivals and parades go to Party Starter, opera and theatre premieres to On Stage.

themes.name: Live Wire
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of generating, storing or distributing electricity: a battery, generator, power station, grid or renewable source (lamps and nuclear plants excepted)
themes.boundary: Live Wire: electric power and its grids; lamps and Volta's pile go to Let There Be Light, nuclear stations to Atoms for Peace, discoveries about electricity itself to Eureka Moments.

themes.name: The Crusades
themes.scope: Yes if it is a campaign, battle, treaty or military order of the Crusades to the Holy Land, 1095 to 1291, sieges excepted
themes.boundary: The Crusades: Holy Land crusades; the sieges of Antioch, Jerusalem, Acre and Constantinople already in Under Siege stay there, the caliphs to The Caliphs, Clermont's pope is shared with Habemus Papam.
example_beats: Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty (1229)

themes.name: Beyond the Stars
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark science fiction or fantasy book, story or magazine for adult readers
themes.boundary: Beyond the Stars: speculative writing; horror goes to Fright Night, children's fantasy to Bedtime Stories, real space exploration to Other Worlds.
example_beats: Verne's From the Earth to the Moon (1865)
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (1978)

themes.name: Buddha's Path
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in the life of the Buddha or the spread of Buddhism
themes.boundary: Buddha's Path: Buddhism's story; Nalanda stays with Places of Learning, Borobudur with Indonesia, Xuanzang's journey with Silk Road, other faiths' foundings to Faith Founded.
example_beats: Altan Khan names the first Dalai Lama (1578)

themes.name: Made by Machine
themes.scope: Yes if it is a power source, machine tool or factory method that changed how goods are made (textile machines and self-acting robots excepted)
themes.boundary: Made by Machine: engines, machine tools and factories; textile machines go to Spun Yarn, robots and governors to Automata, steel for skyscrapers to Tallest in the World.

themes.name: Wonder Drugs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a medicine or drug class being isolated, invented or first used (vaccines and psychiatric drugs excepted)
themes.boundary: Wonder Drugs: medicines; vaccines and the drugs that ended epidemics go to Plague Years, anaesthetics to Under the Knife, psychiatric drugs to Inside the Mind.
example_beats: Insulin first used on a patient (1922)

themes.name: Look It Up
themes.scope: Yes if it is the first publication of a famous dictionary, encyclopedia, almanac, guidebook or other reference work
themes.boundary: Look It Up: reference works in print; newspapers go to Front Pages, the typefaces they are set in to Letters & Type, Wikipedia to Going Online.

themes.name: Native Nations
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act, treaty, battle or leader of an Indigenous nation north of Mexico, from Cahokia to the present
themes.boundary: Native Nations: Indigenous peoples of the US and Canada; Mesoamerica and the Andes go to Before Columbus, the Spanish conquest to Conquistadors, the Pueblo Revolt stays here rather than in Rise Up!

themes.name: The Ballot Box
themes.scope: Yes if it is a country's first free, multiparty or universal-suffrage election, or a new way of voting, before 2000 (women's suffrage excepted)
themes.boundary: The Ballot Box: elections and voting methods; women winning the vote go to Votes for Women, South Africa's 1994 vote to Against Apartheid, constitutions to Founding Documents.
example_beats: First ostracism vote in Athens (487 BC)

themes.name: Toy Box
themes.scope: Yes if it is the invention or launch of a toy still sold or remembered today (not a board, card or video game)
themes.boundary: Toy Box: playthings; board and card games go to The Games Board, video games to Insert Coin, skateboards to Board Riders.
example_beats: LEGO brick as we know it (1958)

themes.name: Rise Up!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a rebellion of peasants, slaves or townspeople against their rulers, outside China, rather than a coup or a war between states
themes.boundary: Rise Up!: risings from below; seizures of power from the top go to Coup!, peaceful protest to Take to the Streets, China's great rebellions (Yellow Turban to Taiping) stay with Mandate of Heaven.

themes.name: Opening Whistle
themes.scope: Yes if it is the first staging of a sport's flagship competition that is still held today (a world cup, grand slam, classic race or championship)
themes.boundary: Opening Whistle: first editions; the invention of the sport goes to Rule Book, anything at the Olympics to Gold Medal Moments, later football moments to Beautiful Game.

themes.name: Against Apartheid
themes.scope: Yes if it is a law, protest, trial or political turning point in South Africa's apartheid era, from 1948 to the 1996 constitution
themes.boundary: Against Apartheid: South Africa 1948 to 1996, its 1994 election included; independence elsewhere in Africa goes to Uhuru, the Nobel prizes it won to Nobel Peace Prize.

themes.name: Giant Killers

themes.boundary: Giant Killers: upsets; Olympic ones go to Gold Medal Moments, other football moments to Beautiful Game, small armies beating big ones to Against the Odds.

India wins the Cricket World Cup (1983)

themes.name: Sing Out!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a national anthem, protest song or charity single, dated to when it was written or released

themes.name: Back from the Brink
themes.scope: Yes if it is a law, treaty, park, reserve or rescue that protected wild species or wild places
themes.boundary: Back from the Brink: conservation, national parks included; extinctions go to Gone Forever, Przewalski's horses stay with Tamed, the ozone layer to Heating Up.

themes.name: Prime Time
themes.scope: Yes if it is the debut of a live-action television series or format that became a hit far beyond its home country
themes.boundary: Prime Time: the shows; channels and broadcast technology go to Tune In, animated series to Drawn to Life, Korean dramas to Korean Wave.

themes.scope: Yes if it is a declaration, decisive battle or founding act in the independence wars of Latin America and the Caribbean, 1791 to 1898
